findings.message: AC-5 says HR uses one today, the entity's own. This diff moves addPerson, recordLeaver and applyStatusDates to entityToday(), but changePersonRun still uses UTC today() in two places: the default effective date (line 53) and the 'title, location and work email change today' check (line 58). That leaves two rules for 'today' in one module, and they disagree in the hours when an entity's date is ahead of UTC. Fix: use entityToday(tx, p.legal_entity_id) for both lines. Add a variant test that runs Sri Lanka and Australia at 20:00 UTC with effectiveOn left out, and again with effectiveOn set to the entity's today and a title change.
findings.scenario: At 2026-11-15T20:00Z, add_person adds someone to Sri Lanka. They join on 2026-11-16 (LK today) as active. Right after, change_person moves their department with no effectiveOn. It writes a period effective 2026-11-15, the day before their employment starts. Or change_person sets title with effectiveOn 2026-11-16 (LK today) and is refused with 'title change today'.

findings.message: applyStatusDates skips an entity with no time zone and only lists it in `unzoned`, inside the audit's after. statusDatesJob ignores the result, so the job reports success every hour while people in that entity never change status. Before this change they moved by UTC. The 'not run' state never reaches anyone who could act on it. Fix: when `unzoned` is not empty, make the job fail or raise a notification/flag (for example, throw after the zoned entities are applied, or emit an event a notifications rule picks up). Test that a run with an unzoned entity does not read as a clean success.
findings.scenario: A tenant has an AU entity with no entity_zone row, and someone there has joined_on 2026-11-20 with status 'joining'. From the 20th on, the hourly hr.person.status job succeeds every run, but the person stays 'joining' indefinitely and nothing on screen says why.

findings.message: Two attributions disagree. When the job extends a standing allocation it attributes the write as `allocations.standing for <updated_by>` (line 56). When it ends one, it passes a bare `allocations.standing`. setStanding writes that value into the ended standing row's updated_by and into the allocationSet event's `by`, so the end loses which person the standing allocation was set for. Fix: pass `allocations.standing for ${s.updated_by}` to endSlot. For the leaver handler, name the person for whom the leaver was recorded where known.
findings.scenario: Maya sets a standing allocation on GONE, and GONE closes. After the monthly job runs, the standing row's updated_by and the event's `by` read 'allocations.standing', with no person.

findings.message: monthRange formats any two months without checking their order. If Through is edited to a month before the start, the button reads as a range of about a year in the forward direction. The service later refuses the input ('through can't be before month'). Fix: when `to < from`, return null or show the end as typed, so the label does not name a range that will never be written.
findings.scenario: rangeFrom 2027-03, Through edited to 2027-01 → the button reads 'Add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT, Mar–Jan', which looks like March 2027 to January 2028.

findings.message: zoneNote's catch does not only catch entityOf's 'no legal entity X' and 'ambiguous' refusals. It catches every error, including a failed database query, and returns that error's message as the card note. That contradicts its own doc comment ('a failed query is an error, not a pass') and can put raw database error text on the card. Fix: catch only entityOf's validation errors and rethrow everything else.
findings.scenario: The legal_entity query fails (for example, a statement timeout) → the Add to HR card shows the Postgres error message as its note instead of failing.

findings.message: monthRange names the year only when the two ends' years differ. So a Through earlier than the start, in the same year, shows as 'Mar–Jan'. That reads as a range running into the next year, and the service refuses it ('through can't be before month'). Fix: return null (or a flagged string) when to < from, so the button falls back to the start month plus the value as typed until the field check flags it.
findings.scenario: Range card starting 2027-03, Through edited to 2027-01 → button reads 'Add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT, Mar–Jan', which looks like Mar 2027 to Jan 2028; confirm is refused.

findings.message: linkNote's doc comment says that for an entity with no time zone the note says 'today there is UTC's'. Since round 2 the note is the refusal (noZone) or the entity-lookup error. Fix the comment to match.
